commitResults.messageTitle: Enforce unique applicant names and emails
commitResults.messageBody:
Applicants can share an email despite the feature specification
requiring both names and emails to be unique.

Reject conflicts when adding, editing, or loading applicants while
preserving identity matching for linked applications. Exclude the
applicant being edited when checking other records for conflicts.

Add regression coverage and document the uniqueness requirements.

Validation: 366 tests, Checkstyle, coverage, and formatting pass.

Deleting an applicant replaces their details with another selection
or an empty panel, preventing users from reviewing what was removed.

Display a snapshot of the deleted applicant and former application,
clearly marked as deleted. Clear the list selection and restore the
normal details view on subsequent applicant actions.

Cover command results, cascading deletion, and UI transitions, and
document the deletion behavior.

Validation: 359 tests, Checkstyle, coverage, and formatting pass.
Chore/add agent skills

commitResults.messageTitle: Preserve deleted details when opening Help
commitResults.messageBody:
The help command refreshes applicant selection and hides the deleted
applicant snapshot, while opening Help through the menu preserves it.

Exclude Help results from applicant view updates so both entry points
preserve the snapshot. Add UI regression tests for both entry points
and an empty displayed list, and document the behavior.

Validation: All 362 tests pass on Java 25, along with Checkstyle,
coverage, and repository formatting checks.

commitResults.messageTitle: Update README to match project details
commitResults.messageBody:
The README currently describes the AddressBook sample project.

Replace sample content with LinkedOut's purpose and project direction.
Distinguish implemented functionality from planned recruitment features.

The landing page describes AddressBook and links to its CI status.

Introduce LinkedOut's target users and recruitment workflow, clarify
which features are under development, and point the CI badge to our
repository. Keep the UI image below the badge and retain upstream
attribution.

commitResults.messageTitle: Update developer guide glossary for LinkedOut
commitResults.messageBody:
The glossary contains terminology from the AddressBook template
that does not reflect LinkedOut's applicant tracking features.

Replace the private contact detail entry with definitions for
applicants, applications, job descriptions, statuses, and indices.
Base these definitions on the official Feature Specification tab
and retain Mainstream OS for legacy compatibility.
Clean up About Us page

LinkedOut needs a command to view an applicant, but the parser has no
view route and the dedicated details panel has not been built yet.

Add view INDEX using the existing index parser and command result
display to show the applicant's name and email. Preserve the displayed
list and its filter, and report invalid indices with a usage hint or
valid range.

Keep this first slice independent of hyphen-option parsing and model
changes so the details panel can be introduced in a later PR.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add applicant selection to command results
commitResults.messageBody:
Command results only carry feedback and help or exit actions, so the
UI cannot identify an applicant to select after a command succeeds.

Add an optional applicant selection to command results while preserving
the existing defaults. Cover the new result state in constructor,
equality, and hash code tests.

commitResults.messageTitle: Connect view commands to applicant details
commitResults.messageBody:
The view command prints contact details without updating the selected
applicant, leaving the detail panel out of sync with the command.

Select and scroll to the requested applicant, and show a short
confirmation alongside the detail panel. Preserve filtered list indices
and failed-command selections, with regression coverage for both.

Fixes #68

The view guide describes name and email output in the command result
display, which no longer matches the applicant detail workflow.

Describe list selection, scrolling, and the details shown in the panel.
Include an example that selects an applicant from filtered results.

commitResults.messageTitle: Migrate add to hyphen option syntax
commitResults.messageBody:
The add command uses slash prefixes even though a shared tokenizer
supports hyphen options.

Use that tokenizer to accept short and long aliases for all four
required person fields and reject the legacy add syntax. Preserve field
validation and edit syntax, and update usage hints and test fixtures.

Cover aliases, malformed options, legacy input, and saving a person
through the logic layer.

commitResults.messageTitle: Document the new add command syntax
commitResults.messageBody:
The User Guide still shows slash syntax and tag options for add, which
no longer match the command parser.

Update the quick start, command reference, examples, and summary to use
hyphen options. Explain required fields, long aliases, and validation
rules so users can construct valid add commands.

commitResults.messageTitle: Unlink edit command from MVP user interface
commitResults.messageBody:
The edit command remains reachable and documented even though editing
applicants is outside the MVP.

Remove edit from command dispatch and user-facing documentation.
Preserve its implementation and unit tests so it can return later, and
keep UI update coverage through direct model changes.

Fixes #75

commitResults.messageTitle: Merge master into the command syntax branch
commitResults.messageBody:
Master removes person addresses while this branch introduces hyphen
options for add, so their parsers, fixtures, and documentation conflict.

Preserve master's address removal and keep short and long aliases for
name, phone, and email. Update the affected tests and guide to use the
three-field add command and reject removed address options.

Validate with Java 25 using Gradle check and coverage, including the
JavaFX integration tests under Xvfb.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add shared agent guidance and coding standards
commitResults.messageBody:
The brownfield project needs shared guidance for AI-assisted changes
and consistent Java and Git conventions across contributors.

Add repository-wide agent instructions, local SE-EDU skills, and a
commit-message validation hook. Track the guidance files so agents
and contributors use the same rules as the project evolves.

Retain the Java 25 requirement and macOS setup command while referring
to the README and build configuration for changing project details.

commitResults.messageTitle: Document hook setup and validation coverage
commitResults.messageBody:
The shared commit-message hook needs per-clone configuration, and
contributors need to know which conventions it checks automatically.

Document the local hook setup and distinguish automated formatting
checks from rules requiring manual review. Clarify the hook's scope
without changing its validation behavior.
